title: Oral Health Misinformation on Youtube - A Content Analysis.
screen_reason: CONTENT prevalence available from the abstract: 72 oral-health YouTube videos were each classified by two coders as accurate (useful) or misleading, and about 55% were misleading - a share of items with a stated denominator.

estimates.measure_type: % of oral-health YouTube videos classified as containing misleading information rather than accurate (useful) information
estimates.denominator: 72 YouTube videos retrieved with common oral-health keywords (Chrome incognito search) and included after screening
estimates.definition: Two coders examined the auditory and visual content of each video together using a coding framework and classified every video as either accurate information (useful) or misleading information; the numerator is the videos classified misleading
estimates.misinfo_def: “All the videos were classified either as accurate information (useful) or misleading information.”
estimates.source_quote: A total of 72 videos were included in the study, of which about 55% of them had misleading content.
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Two coders examined auditory and visual content together using a coding framework; the abstract reports no inter-rater reliability statistic, no coder credentials and no external reference standard.
estimates.moderator_quote: A search was done on YouTube using common keywords related to oral health through Google chrome browser with incognito mode to limit the bias associated with Google accounts. The videos obtained were subjected to analysis using a coding framework and both auditory and visual content were examined together by two coders to ensure a comprehensive coding process.
estimates.notes: ABSTRACT-ONLY extraction; no methods or results section was available. The value is reported as 'about 55%', i.e. an author-rounded figure with no numerator count (0.55 x 72 = 39.6 videos, so the underlying count is 39 or 40); kept because it is stated verbatim, but treat the second digit as approximate. year left blank: neither a data-collection period nor a publication year appears anywhere in the text file, and the blindness rule forbids looking it up. borderline=true is set for the denom_selection call, not the construct: a keyword YouTube search yielding 72 videos is almost certainly rank-truncated, so I coded denom_selection=curated per the multi-keyword / top-N rule, but the abstract never states a top-N cut, so an adjudicator could defensibly leave it blank. The construct itself is not in doubt - videos were judged accurate vs misleading, a veracity classification, not a DISCERN- style quality score.

missed_or_uncertain: Numbers seen but NOT extracted. (a) 'About 75% of the videos containing misleading information were created by non-professionals and only about 15% of the videos containing misleading information were created by medical professionals' - these are creator-attribution shares computed inside the misleading-only subsample (denominator = the ~40 misleading videos), not a share of content that is false, so R3's within_misinfo_content rule does not apply (that rule covers falsity measured inside a misinformation-only sample) and they are not prevalence estimates. They also do not sum to 100%, implying a third creator category that the abstract does not name. (b) Engagement totals - misleading 137,429 vs useful 71,207 positive engagement - are raw counts with no denominator, so no row. (c) No country, no data-collection window, no keyword list, no reliability statistic and no per-keyword or per-subtopic breakdown are available from the abstract; a full text would likely support a stricter definition variant and possibly subtopic rows.

rob.design: Cross-sectional content analysis, abstract only. YouTube searched with 'common keywords related to oral health' in Google Chrome incognito mode to limit account personalisation; 72 videos included. Both auditory and visual content examined together by two coders using a coding framework, each video classified as accurate (useful) or misleading. No sampling frame size, no search date, no country, no inter-rater reliability statistic and no coder qualifications are reported in the abstract; not a survey, so no response rate.
rob.item6_quote: All the videos were classified either as accurate information (useful) or misleading information.
rob.item10_quote: A total of 72 videos were included in the study, of which about 55% of them had misleading content.
